goal: Andrea's Resort is a lakeside cabin property with a perfect 5.0 Google rating, a working online booking system and 37 strong photos on its website. What it does not have is visibility. There are only 20 reviews, 522 followers across Instagram and Facebook, and one social post every ten weeks.

Over the next 90 days the goal is to increase direct bookings by 50% and grow the social following past 1,000, by posting consistently, building a steady flow of new reviews, and making the resort easy to find in local search.
positioning: Most cabin properties in the region compete on price or on the size of the hot tub. Andrea's Resort competes on calm: a quiet stretch of lakefront, cabins that are properly looked after, and owners who answer the phone.
strategy.positioning_statement: Andrea's Resort is the lakeside escape for families and couples who want a peaceful, nature-first getaway with modern comforts and personal hospitality. Every post, review reply and web page should sound like the owners talking, and should show the lake.
strategy.welcome_message: You already deliver a five-star stay. This plan is about making sure the people planning their next trip can see that before they book somewhere else.

objectives.title: Build Social Presence
objectives.description: A consistent, engaging social presence that shows the cabin experience and reaches new audiences.

objectives.title: Grow Review Momentum
objectives.description: A steady flow of recent reviews that builds trust and improves local ranking.

objectives.title: Lead Local Search
objectives.description: A complete Google profile, consistent listings and useful pages that capture people ready to book.

objectives.title: Win Direct Bookings
objectives.description: A booking path with no friction and an email list of guests who want to come back.

tactics.title: Social Media Activation
tactics.subtitle: Build a consistent, engaging presence that drives discovery and turns followers into guests.
what_we_heard: You have beautiful cabin photography and guests who love their stay, but your social accounts do not show it. With 194 followers on Instagram, 328 on Facebook and one post every ten weeks, the accounts look closed. You told us the blocker is time, not ideas.
what_this_is: A four-week sprint that takes your social media from dormant to active. You will set a posting rhythm, turn the photos you already own into a month of posts in one sitting, start publishing short video, and build the small daily habits that grow an audience.
why_it_matters: Leisure travellers find places to stay on Instagram and Facebook before they ever search Google. A quiet account suggests a quiet business. Three posts a week for twelve weeks beats ten posts in one burst followed by a month of silence.

steps.title: Fix both profiles before you post anything

items.text: On Instagram, tap **Edit profile** and rewrite the bio to say what the resort is and where it is, including the drive time from the nearest city.
Add the direct booking link in the **Links** field. It is currently empty, which is why the account has produced no website clicks.
Add four story highlights:
Repeat the bio and booking link on the Facebook page.

media.alt: Instagram profile with the new bio, location and booking link
media.caption: Updated bio with location and booking link

steps.title: Set a fixed weekly pattern

items.text: Monday is a cabin feature, Wednesday is a local activity, Friday is a guest experience.
Block 30 minutes every Sunday to check the week ahead.
Write the pattern down and share it with whoever else might post. A pattern only one person knows stops when that person is busy.

media.alt: A one-page weekly posting pattern: cabin feature Monday, local activity Wednesday, guest experience Friday

parts.name: Create a Month of Content in One Sitting

steps.title: Sort the 37 website photos into the three themes

items.text: Create three folders named `cabins`, `activities` and `guests`.
Aim for at least four photos in each folder. If the guest folder is thin, ask three recent guests for permission to share theirs.

steps.title: Write 12 captions and schedule them in Meta Business Suite

items.text: Open [Meta Business Suite](https://business.facebook.com/) and choose **Planner**, then **Schedule post**.
Write captions that tell a short story instead of describing the photo.
Say where the resort is at least once a week.
Publish each post to Instagram and Facebook together, not separately.

media.alt: The Meta Business Suite planner with scheduled posts

steps.title: Publish two Reels a week

items.text: Keep each one under 30 seconds and shoot it vertically on a phone.
Start with formats that need no editing: a walk through a cabin, the dock at sunrise, the fire pit at night.
Quiet footage with natural sound works well for this kind of property.

media.alt: Vertical Reel walking through a cabin interior
Vertical Reel of the dock and the lake at sunrise

steps.title: Reply to every comment within two hours during the day

items.text: Turn on notifications for comments and messages on both accounts.
Follow 50 local accounts: the regional tourism office, nearby restaurants and activity operators.

tips: Post when your audience is online: 7 to 9 in the morning and 7 to 9 in the evening.
Follower count matters less than engagement rate and website clicks. A small audience that responds books more often than a large one that scrolls past.
If a week gets away from you, post one photo of the lake with one honest sentence. Keeping the rhythm matters more than the quality of any single post.

tactics.title: Review Generation
tactics.subtitle: Turn happy guests into steady, recent reviews.
what_we_heard: You have a perfect 5.0 on Google, but only 20 reviews, and almost none from this year. You have never asked guests for one because it felt awkward.
what_this_is: A simple system that asks every guest once, at the right moment, and makes it take under a minute.
why_it_matters: Review count and recency both affect local ranking. A property with 70 recent reviews at 4.8 outranks one with 20 older reviews at 5.0.

steps.title: Create your Google review link

items.text: In your Google Business Profile, choose **Ask for reviews** and copy the short link.

steps.title: Send a review request three days after checkout

items.text: Keep the email to three sentences: thank them, ask, give the link.
Set it up as an automation in your booking system so it does not depend on memory.

media.alt: A three-sentence review request email with a Google review link
media.caption: Review request: sent three days after checkout

confirm.text: Which booking system the resort uses

steps.title: Put a QR card in every cabin

items.text: Place it beside the checkout instructions.

media.alt: A printed QR code card on a table beside the checkout instructions
media.caption: QR card beside the checkout instructions

steps.title: Reply within 24 hours and mention something specific

items.text: Thank the guest by name, mention one detail from their stay and invite them back.
Reply to the 20 existing reviews first. None of them has a response.

tips: Never offer a discount or gift for a review. It breaks Google's rules and guests can tell.

tactics.title: Local Search Visibility and the Pages That Earn Search Traffic All Year
tactics.subtitle: Be the first result when someone nearby searches for a lakeside cabin.
what_we_heard: Your Google Business Profile is verified but barely used. The website has no structured data, the homepage title is cut off in search results, and the resort is missing from most tourism directories. You also told us that guests ask the same five questions by email every week.
what_this_is: Twelve weeks of small, specific jobs: complete the Google profile, fix the technical basics on the website, list the resort consistently across directories, and publish the pages that answer what guests already ask.
why_it_matters: Someone searching "lakeside cabin near me" is ready to book. Local search is where the resort's perfect rating can do the most work, and right now very few people see it.

steps.title: Fill in every section of the profile

items.text: Add seasonal opening dates, check-in hours, amenities and the booking link.
Choose **Cabin rental agency** as the primary category and **Resort hotel** as a secondary one.

items.text: Add exterior, interior, lake and winter photos. Profiles with recent photos get more direction requests.
Publish one Google Post a week tied to whatever is live on the website.

items.text: Keep the title under 60 characters, for example `Andrea's Resort | Lakeside Cabins for Families and Couples`.
Break the homepage into sections with headings: Cabins, The Lake, Getting Here, Things To Do.

steps.title: Add structured data

items.text: Ask your web developer to add `LocalBusiness` and `LodgingBusiness` schema with the name, address, phone number and hours.
Check the result in the [Rich Results Test](https://search.google.com/test/rich-results).

steps.title: Audit your existing listings

items.text: Search the resort name and note every listing on the first three pages.
Record the name, address and phone number each one shows. They must match exactly, character for character.

parts.name: Publish the Pages Guests Already Ask For

steps.title: Write a Know Before You Go page

items.text: Answer the five questions you get every week:

children.text: How far is it from the highway?
Where is the nearest grocery store?

items.text: Add the page to the main menu the same day you publish it.

steps.title: Publish one local guide a month

items.text: Start with a three-day itinerary, then a rainy-day guide, then a winter guide.
End every guide with a link to the booking page.

steps.title: Record a baseline in Google Search Console

items.text: Export the last three months of clicks and impressions before you change anything.

steps.title: Review local ranking every month

items.text: Search your three most important phrases from a private browser window and note where the resort appears.

tips: Name, address and phone number must match everywhere. "Rd" in one listing and "Road" in another counts as a mismatch.
Answer every question on the Google profile within a day. Unanswered questions stay visible to everyone.
Every question a guest asks twice is a page worth writing.

tactics.title: Direct Booking and Guest Email
tactics.subtitle: Make booking direct the easiest option, and stay in touch with guests who have already stayed.
what_we_heard: Most of your bookings come through third-party sites that take a commission, even from guests who found you by name. You have email addresses for several years of past guests and have never written to them.
what_this_is: Two connected pieces of work: remove the friction from booking on your own website, and start a small, respectful email program for past guests.
why_it_matters: Every booking that moves from a third-party site to your own website keeps the commission in the business. Past guests are the cheapest bookings you will ever get, because they already know the place.

steps.title: Put a Book Now button in the site header

items.text: It should appear on every page and open the booking page directly, not a contact form.

media.alt: The site header with a Book Now button
media.caption: Book Now in the header on every page

steps.title: Show rates, cabin types and the cancellation policy on the booking page

items.text: Guests leave when they have to email to ask a price.
Put the full cancellation policy on the page itself.

steps.title: Import past guests and ask permission

items.text: Export guest emails from your booking system and send one short message asking them to confirm they want to hear from you.
Keep only the people who confirm. A small confirmed list is worth more than a large unconfirmed one.

steps.title: Add a sign-up form to the website footer

items.text: Give a specific reason to subscribe, such as first notice of summer dates.

steps.title: Build the pre-arrival email

items.text: Send it five days before arrival with directions, check-in details and what to bring.

media.alt: A pre-arrival email with directions, check-in details and what to bring
media.caption: Pre-arrival email: sent five days before check-in

steps.title: Send one seasonal availability email

items.text: Share which dates are still open and link straight to the booking page.
Send it to past guests only, once, and measure bookings in the following two weeks.

tips: Describe the emails to guests as service, not marketing: one before they arrive and one when dates open.
Offer something small for booking direct, such as a late checkout, and say so beside the Book Now button.
